followup_reviews.Research finding: The July 2017 bagayeros protest is supported as an included, intermittent trade-route restriction distinct from later Yacuiba disputes. Freight in both directions was obstructed, with negotiated perishable-cargo passage. The record does not claim that every passenger or every commodity was continuously blocked. The contemporary 21 July interview anchors Monday onset to 17 July. Lifting notification on 25 July and actual passage in a 26 July report with an unspecified day support existing 25–26 July return bounds. Preserve intermittent_regime, withheld_intermittent, null duration and zero complete flags. Separate 18:30/19:30 accounts do not form a proven same-day clock sequence. Trade and protectionism / Trade and transport protests remains supported by named bagayeros leaders’ demands for customs treatment comparable with large importers and the associated livelihood claim. The Erbol/Radio Parapetí interview was freshly read. Nizkor’s explicitly attributed El Tribuno report and the IBCE digest were reread from exact saved passages. The mirror is not independent of El Tribuno; the digest’s unnamed originating paper is not guessed from its URL. The bridge and immediate access remain unlocated; no blockade-point coordinate or continuous animation is inferred from the named place and overall protest dates.
